newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Stan Chart may ally with European banks.
newsitem.headline: Stan Chart may ally with European banks.

text.p: Standard Chartered Plc chief executive officer Malcolm Williamson said on Wednesday his bank was discussing possible alliances with more than five European banks and hoped to be able to make an announcement on one of them in the next one or two months.
Williamson told Reuters in an interview these alliances would allow Standard Chartered to offer use of its financial services in Asia to banks which did not have an Asian presence.

"We have announced deals so far with a number of banks, four in North America and one in Australia and we are in the course of discussion with quite a number of other banks in other parts of the OECD," he said.
"We haven't announced any in Europe yet but we are in quite detailed discussions with a number of people."

"We have five deals up and running now and we've got considerably more than that under discussion. Just when they'll come to fruitition and when we will be able to announce them, I wouldn't like to predict...I hope within the next month or two."
"These things sometimes take some time to put together because they are very much bespoke arrangements," he added.
In 1996, Standard Chartered formed joint ventures in Asia with Westpac Banking Corp, First Chicago NBD Corp and Massachusetts-based Fleet Financial Services.
Williamson said alliances with other banks offered potential gains for both sides.

"What we are saying to them is, 'Look we have a huge infrastructure in Asia, we are in every country except North Korea. You are not in Asia and its going to be expensive to get there if you want to. Why don't you use us as if we were a branch network extension?'," he said.
"We can wire them up with technology so that we can appear as if we were just an extension of (their) financial services," he said.
"It works extremely well for them. They get a very good service for their customers and it gets more business through our branches so we benefit from lower business costs," he said.
